intention: Make the nightly Supercharger path incremental: updated_at must mean 'this row's data changed' at the telemetry and charging layers, the telemetry->charging mirror read must be watermark-bounded, and every telemetry query and Fleet API call must log its arguments.
request: Source ticket: MAG-48 - Nightly Reconcile recalculates the whole vehicle_metrics history on every poller run. Measured 2026-09-05: 70-day window and 51/51 metric rows rewritten where the snapshot source alone needed 4 days. Owner added two scope items beyond the original bug: bound the O(all-history) mirror read, and log every telemetry query + Fleet API call with its input arguments.

decisions.decision: Three-layer cascade; internal/analytics is NOT changed
decisions.why: Layer 3's filter shape is already correct - it is only ever fed lies by layers 1 and 2

decisions.decision: updated_at must mean 'this row's data changed' on both supercharger tables
decisions.why: An unchanged mirror pass must stop widening the window, while a real human battery-% edit must still trigger it

decisions.decision: The change comparison is structural, never a hand-listed WHERE predicate; includes tesla_id, excludes the human-owned columns
decisions.why: A future column added to the SET but forgotten in a hand-listed WHERE would silently stop advancing updated_at - the original objection

decisions.decision: The mirror's cursor is a charging-owned watermark table holding telemetry's updated_at
decisions.why: A cursor belongs to the module that reads, never the one that is read; sharing analytics' cursor loses data because the two track different tables

decisions.decision: CRITICAL: the watermark never advances to now() on an empty read - only to the max updated_at observed, untouched when zero rows return
decisions.why: A row committed one second late would sit permanently behind the cursor and never be mirrored - silent, undetectable data loss

decisions.decision: The bounded read reuses the 24h overlap guard (updated_at >= cursor - 24h)
decisions.why: Same commit-skew reason recalcOverlap exists in analytics; the idempotent upsert makes the re-read a no-op

decisions.decision: Logging is an explicit, non-embedding decorator mirroring internal/telemetry/call_counter.go
decisions.why: Embedding would let a method added later satisfy the type by promotion and go silently unlogged

decisions.decision: Keep stdlib log.Printf with new 'telemetry query:' / 'fleet api:' prefixes; do NOT introduce slog
decisions.why: The repo has zero slog and 40+ log.Printf lines; a second logging library inside a bug fix is out of scope

decisions.decision: Never log a credential or a raw_data blob; enforced structurally and asserted by a test
decisions.why: Every Fleet API method takes tesla.Credentials, so a naive 'log the arguments' leaks a live bearer token

decisions.decision: Unit tests ARE included in every tier
decisions.why: User was asked and changed the standing 'no unit tests' default; D3's comparison and D5's empty-read rule are exactly what a test must pin

decisions.decision: Tier order: logging first; the updated_at work splits across tiers 2 and 3
decisions.why: The tier-1 instrument is what makes tiers 2-4 provable rather than theoretical; the split is forced by the one-module-per-worker sandbox

decisions.decision: Every LIVE telemetry query is already behind an interface (store x3, Reader x5, SuperchargerHistoryReader x4, RunWriter x1) - decorate those four, no call-site logging needed
decisions.why: service.go:42's store seam already covers the three 'internal' writes; the ticket's premise that 5 queries sit behind no interface was wrong

decisions.decision: DELETE ListSnapshotsByVehicle and ListPollAttemptsByVehicle; rewrite the 10 integration-test call sites on raw SQL, never on another sqlc reader query
decisions.why: They have no production caller. Reusing a live reader would make a test verify through the path it tests; raw SQL keeps the assertion independent

decisions.decision: Fleet API logging EXTENDS the existing callCounter rather than adding a sibling decorator
decisions.why: One type, one compile-time assertion, one place a new Fleet API method must be added - no chaining order to get wrong

decisions.decision: The structural comparison is a to_jsonb DENY-LIST inside the ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE: to_jsonb(tbl.*) - deny IS DISTINCT FROM to_jsonb(EXCLUDED.*) - deny. Trigger and ROW() allow-list both rejected.
decisions.why: Deny-list fails LOUD (a forgotten column over-updates, the known symptom); an allow-list fails SILENT, which is what D3 forbids. Verified on PG16; sqlc parses it with no Go signature change.

decisions.decision: Each tier ships a self-checking DB test that reads the table's real columns from information_schema, writes a non-default sentinel into every column the upsert does not write, re-runs the identical upsert, and asserts updated_at did not move.
decisions.why: Turns the deny-list's runtime-only failure into a deterministic test signal: adding a table column fails the test until the deny-list is updated. Zero maintenance after.

decisions.decision: Tiers 2 and 3 run IN PARALLEL - one worker per module, both design gates presented together, one suite run, two reviewers.
decisions.why: internal/telemetry and internal/charging are disjoint in files and both depend only on tier 1. Halves wall-clock and shares the test round-trips.

decisions.decision: The comparison covers EXACTLY the columns the ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET writes. The deny-list is the complement of the SET clause: telemetry 16 names (6 compared), charging 14 names (5 compared). The SET clause itself is NOT widened - write-once columns keep today's behaviour.
decisions.why: Leader proved on live PG16 that a write-once column drifting at the source advances updated_at while the stored value stays old, so the difference never resolves and that row churns every night forever. Live risk: unlatch_date_time NULL in 2 of 8 rows.

decisions.decision: DATABASE DESIGN GATE CONFIRMED for both tiers. Implementation may start.
decisions.why: Owner reviewed the design, rationale, rejected alternatives and index plan (no new index in either tier) and confirmed both.

decisions.decision: Add SuperchargerHistoryByAccountUpdatedSince(accountID, since) to telemetry's SuperchargerHistoryReader. Tier 4 therefore touches internal/telemetry as well as internal/charging.
decisions.why: The mirror reads per account; the only updated-since query is per vehicle and filters tesla_id = X, so it can never return a tesla_id NULL row - exactly the orphan-recovery path D3 protects.

decisions.decision: The table is charging.mirror_watermarks(id, account_id UNIQUE, source_updated_at, created_at, updated_at). No tesla_id, no source column. UNIQUE(account_id) serves the only read; no separate index.
decisions.why: The mirror read is account-wide, not per vehicle, and charging mirrors exactly one upstream table. A second source later is an additive migration.

decisions.decision: internal/app orchestrates: read cursor, read telemetry since cursor-24h, MirrorSessions, advance to max observed updated_at. charging gains MirrorWatermark + AdvanceMirrorWatermark. MirrorSessions' signature is UNCHANGED.
decisions.why: Keeping the signature saves ~19 test call sites plus the fake. A crash between mirror and advance leaves the cursor behind - repeated work, never lost rows.

decisions.decision: Tier 4 stays ONE change, RM44-charging-add-mirror-watermark, implemented by two module workers (telemetry, then charging) and reviewed by one reviewer per module. No tier 5 is added.
decisions.why: The telemetry part is one query, one reader method and one decorator line. A second full cycle - gate, reviewer, archive, spec sync - is not proportionate to ~60 lines.

decisions.decision: REVISES D23. Tier 4's change is renamed RM44-platform-add-mirror-watermark and archives under archive/platform/. Still ONE change, two module workers, two reviewers.
decisions.why: openspec/config.yaml forbids a change spanning two modules but offers the platform- prefix for cross-cutting work. The rename uses that escape instead of bending the rule.

decisions.decision: DATABASE DESIGN GATE CONFIRMED for tier 4, with one change: ship idx_supercharger_history_account_updated (account_id, updated_at) now, in a telemetry migration.
decisions.why: Owner chose certainty over a possible slow-query investigation later. The design had recommended documenting it as a revisit trigger instead; both positions are recorded.
